prompt: Using streams, find the most common word in a text: lowercase it, split on non-letters, count with Collectors.groupingBy + counting, and break count ties alphabetically. Return "" when there are no words.
explanation: Two pipelines do the work. The first tokenizes: split("[^a-z]+") on the lowercased text breaks it at every run of non-letters (a leading empty token is filtered out), and groupingBy with the counting() downstream collector produces a Map<String, Long> of word frequencies in one pass. The second pipeline streams the map entries with a composed comparator -- count descending via comparingByValue().reversed(), then key ascending for ties -- so findFirst() yields the champion and orElse("") covers the no-words case.
hints: Start with java.util.Arrays.stream(text.toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT).split("[^a-z]+")) and filter out empty strings.
Collect with Collectors.groupingBy(w -> w, Collectors.counting()) to get a Map<String, Long> of frequencies.
Stream counts.entrySet(), sort with Map.Entry.<String, Long>comparingByValue().reversed().thenComparing(Map.Entry.comparingByKey()), then map to getKey and use findFirst().orElse("").
